To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
priming of visual word form is associated with a positive offset of brain potentials recorded in the occipital-parietal region of the brain.
the ERP offset difference observed during the repetition of words in the backward and forward formats is an index of priming, and that this effect is dissociable from explicit remembering.

the ERP response to a word presentation is different if the word has appeared earlier in the backward format compared to the forward format, and that this difference is observed only when the task is a word discrimination rather than a recognition test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain represents and processes information in memory, and how this information can be retrieved from memory.
the study of brain potentials associated with the processing of visual information, and with the neural mechanisms of visual priming.
the neural mechanisms underlying perceptual and conceptual priming in reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N250 is an ERP index of the neural processes underlying perceptual priming, and that the N400 is an index of the neural process underlying explicit remembering.
the ERP difference observed in Experiment 1 reflects a process that is specific to the perceptual processing of visual word form, and is not a general effect of perceptual priming.
the N400 is not a unitary phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERP measures are sensitive to neural events associated with the specific influence of reading experiences on the visual processing of word-form.
primed words are recognized faster and earlier, and this effect may be mediated by a more efficient perceptual analysis of the visual input.
the repetition of visual form of words is associated with a positive offset ERP component, and this ERP component is associated with perceptual learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural mechanisms underlying priming can be investigated by recording brain activity while subjects perform a reading manipulation in the laboratory.
ERP measures are useful in the study of priming and other forms of implicit memory.
the brain is sensitive to the perceptual properties of the words that we see, and that this perceptual sensitivity can be measured with ERPs.
